rites.name: Thosten
rites.text: Thosten is the concept of the Ki Realm's Courts, the principle by which contested oaths are weighed and sealed in Coreoserus. In the first age of divine trials, Thosten was the measure every council used to decide which doors between worlds would hold.

rites.name: Lyinnys
rites.text: Lyinnys is the concept of a binding oath sworn before the Courts of Coreoserus, held to be the reason a trial could not be undone once it was judged. In the Holy Age its devotees carried it as a rule about flame and promise, so that a sealed word burned into the record and could not be recalled.

rites.name: Shyuzis
rites.text: Shyuzis is a concept of Coreoserus, the quiet thread the makers weave into the Seeding while sleeping powers wait in the soil. It belongs to the first age of sovereigns, when groves and growing kingdoms rise around the planted Weave.

rites.name: Gathar
rites.text: Gathar is a concept within Coreoserus, born in the Fall of the Ki Realm during the Sundering, when worlds broke apart and the Shards scattered across the void. It is remembered as the force that held the broken worlds steady long enough for the Pact to be sworn.

rites.name: Miarionnys
rites.text: Miarionnys is a concept of the Ki realm, the living current that the sovereigns of Coreoserus learned to braid into groves and growing kingdoms. It is remembered as the thread that held the Pact together when the Sundering split the worlds and the Shards scattered across the void.

rites.name: Amisteontia
rites.text: A flashy finishing technique that lets a victor unleash a long chain of blows upon a fallen rival until the foe is destroyed in a dazzling display. Some versions alter how the tale concludes, and certain rhythmic chimes echo the fight's music.

rites.name: Terium
rites.text: Terium is a concept born in Coreoserus during the Walled Age, when the builders of holding walls and the first orders of sworn keepers gave it shape. It was held as the force that lets a grove of roots keep its hold through a storm and lets a sovereign's wall stand against the sea.

rites.name: Soleornus
rites.text: A powerful enhanced technique that a fighter unleashes, leaving a dark, trailing afterimage behind them. Its method of execution shifts across different eras of the craft, yet it always marks a formidable strike.

rites.name: Miraustanum
rites.text: A fighter can interrupt an incoming chain of strikes by releasing a special counter-maneuver. The maneuver breaks the opponent's sequence and frees the fighter from it.

rites.name: Oreosor
rites.text: A brief window of helplessness follows a badly timed defensive answer, during which the attacker may strike freely. A stronger counter answer lengthens this frozen span.

rites.name: Laustosium
rites.text: A tally that climbs with every strike in a chain, limiting how long a sequence may run. Once it overflows, the attacker is forced to end the sequence and leaves the foe with a brief window of recoverable harm.

rites.name: Causes
rites.text: A devastating technique a fighter unleashes by spending stored energy from a gauge. It grants a decisive advantage in combat.

rites.name: Meontor
rites.text: A fighter unlocks this strong technique right after escaping a chain of attacks. It rewards a well-timed counter with a powerful follow-up move.

rites.name: Neolanum Telisium
rites.text: A dramatic closing sequence that a victor may unleash when a rival's final health bar flashes its warning state. It ends the fight with a theatrical flourish rather than a simple defeat.

rites.name: Sasellor
rites.text: A fighter channels a rush of inner energy that strengthens their abilities. Every combatant is able to call upon this technique in battle.

rites.name: Telernorium
rites.text: A fighter's system for chaining strikes into extended assaults. It begins with an opener, links through a paired strike and a linker, and closes with a finisher that cashes out the damage. Only a counter-burst can free a victim from the chain.

rites.name: Ternia
rites.text: A defensive technique open to every fighter, letting them absorb an incoming blow and answer it with a predetermined striking maneuver.

rites.name: Oresanum
rites.text: Oresanum is a concept of crystallized ember-stone that hums with a stored, living heat, used by the lamp-smiths of the Ki realm to kindle their age-old night-lanterns. Its power is a quiet one, released slowly through cracks in the rock where its glow seeps into the surrounding soil.

rites.name: Vanavaruta
rites.text: Vanavaruta is a concept of the Coreoserus omniverse, the idea of a single branching choice that the Library files among its shelves of outcomes. It is said to hold the shape of every future that was not chosen, and to hum faintly in the groves during the early years of the first sovereign.

rites.name: Osatheth
rites.text: Osatheth is a concept of Coreoserus, the principle that an ending may branch into many futures, which the Library of the Three Futures shelves side by side. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between peoples, Osatheth was invoked to hold open the choices that remained.
